subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If ax²+2hxy+by²+2gx+2fy+c=0 represents two parallel lines then prove that (i) h²=ab (ii) af²=bg² (iii) the distance between the parallel lines is 2√((g²−ac)/(a(a+b))) or 2√((f²−bc)/(b(a+b))).

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what is special about how you split a PARALLEL pair, and how you get the distance.

steps.label: Split into two PARALLEL lines
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the key step of the question. Parallel lines can be written with the same x and y coefficients, differing ONLY in the constant — so both factors get the same l and m.

y gives m(n₁ + n₂) = 2f, constant n₁n₂ = c)

lines: On equating like term coeff., we get
a = l²,  b = m²,  h = lm,  2g = l(n₁ + n₂),

recall.must_convey: That parallel lines are written with the SAME l and m in both factors, differing only in n.

only the constants differ between the two lines
a is l squared, b is m squared, h is l m

steps.why: This single choice — same l and m in both factors — is what forces every one of the three results that follow. Nothing else in the answer is really new.
common_mistakes: Using different coefficients in the two factors, which describes intersecting lines.
Writing h = 2lm instead of h = lm.
steps.memory_tip: PARALLEL lines share their x and y coefficients and differ only in the CONSTANT — same l and m in both.

steps.label: Prove h² = ab
steps.margin_note: One mark. The first result is immediate from the matched coefficients: h is lm, and a and b are l² and m².

lines.text: (square h = lm, then put l² = a and m² = b)

recall.must_convey: That h = lm gives h² = l²m² = ab.
accept: h is l m so h squared is l squared m squared which is a b
square the h relation and read off a and b
h squared equals a b follows straight from the matched coefficients
h square chesthe a b vasthundi
this proves the first part

steps.why: For a pair of lines, h² = ab holds exactly when the lines are parallel or coincident, and here it follows directly from the splitting.
common_mistakes: Concluding h² > ab, which describes two distinct intersecting lines.
steps.memory_tip: Straight from the matched coefficients: h is lm, and a and b are l² and m².

steps.label: Prove af² = bg²
steps.margin_note: One mark. Both f and g carry the same factor (n₁ + n₂), so squaring each and multiplying by the other's coefficient produces the same expression twice.

recall.must_convey: That af² and bg² both reduce to l²m²(n₁+n₂)²/4, so they are equal.
accept: both sides reduce to the same expression so they are equal
a f squared is l squared times m squared n one plus n two over two all squared
the two sides are the same after expanding
rendu vaipula same expression vasthundi
this proves a f squared equals b g squared

steps.why: f and g differ only in whether they carry m or l, so pairing each with the OTHER letter's square makes the two products identical.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the division by 2 when writing f and g from 2f and 2g.
Pairing a with g² instead of f².
steps.memory_tip: Both f and g carry the same (n₁ + n₂), so each side produces the same expression.

steps.label: Derive the distance
steps.margin_note: The last mark. The two lines share l and m, so the distance is |n₁ − n₂| over √(l² + m²) — and |n₁ − n₂| is found from its square, since only the sum and product of the n's are known.

lines.text: (the distance between parallel lines lx + my + n₁ = 0
((n₁ − n₂)² = (n₁ + n₂)² − 4n₁n₂, and l² + m² = a + b)
and dividing by √(a + b) puts a + b under the root)

recall.must_convey: That the distance is |n₁ − n₂|/√(l² + m²), which converts to 2√((g² − ac)/(a(a+b))).
accept: the distance between parallel lines is the difference of the constants over the root
write n one minus n two through the sum and the product
substitute two g over l for the sum and c for the product
difference of constants over root l square plus m square
this gives the required distance

steps.why: The two stated forms are the SAME distance reached two ways — through g and a, or through f and b — because n₁ + n₂ can be read from either 2g or 2f. The question asks for both.
common_mistakes: Using n₁ + n₂ where |n₁ − n₂| is needed.
Giving only one of the two equivalent forms.
steps.memory_tip: The distance is |n₁ − n₂| over √(l² + m²), and |n₁ − n₂| comes from its SQUARE.

insider_note: Parallel means the two factors share l and m and differ only in the constant; all three parts follow from that one line. The distance needs |n₁ − n₂| via (n₁+n₂)² − 4n₁n₂, and both forms are asked for.
